bullets.text: Companywide Q3 CR was 96.6, bringing YTD to 96.0 through September; Personal Lines Q3 CR was 96.2 (YTD 95.8); Commercial Lines Q3 CR was 99.3 (YTD 94.5); aggregate profit remains first priority.
Companywide NPW +12% and NEP +13% for Q3; Commercial Lines was a key contributor, generating quarter-over-prior-year quarter NPW growth of 21% and NEP growth of 23%.
Added nearly 50% more Robinson (bundled auto-home) policies in Q3 YOY; Robinson retention increased over 10% YOY; solid new policy application growth in Agency and Direct auto channels.
Catastrophes added nearly 3 points to Q3 CR, mainly Louisiana floods (>95% claims closed); early October Hurricane Matthew incurred ~$85M losses with ~60% vehicle and property claims closed.

Commercial Lines took rate and underwriting actions post-haste to meet profit goals; new rates will take time to earn in based on annual policies; Direct auto actions were designed to meet profit goals.
Issued $500M 10-year Senior Notes at 2.45% (92 bps over Treasuries) to support growth within capital policy; investment portfolio fully taxable equivalent total return reached 1.3% in Q3.

Capitalizing on bundled auto-home packages with American Strategic Insurance (ASI); data sharing with ASI peers aims to ascertain bundled package potential; bundled customers demonstrate longer policy life expectancy.

Positioned to leverage dual distribution channel strategy for bundled growth; new business brings higher first-term CR, especially in Direct; Direct auto saw expected deceleration from actions to meet profit goals.

Tricia Griffith assumed leadership; leadership team reported Destination Era progress, citing 'a lot more gas in the tank'; core philosophy remains hitting profit goals first, then growing as fast as possible.

Hiring and training ahead of need enabled customer care during catastrophes, which Progressive believes contributes to retention; recognized Glenn Renwick's 30 years of leadership, including over half as CEO.
